Egypt — 3rd-highest-population country. This round searched explicitly for a genuine sub-governorate (markaz/madina/hay/qism) fiscal tier and confirmed, rather than merely failed to rebut, the existing corpus's (eg-cairo-municipal-finance.json) implicit finding that Egypt's real fiscal-planning tier stops at governorate. A second governorate data point (Luxor) and a richer statutory basis for that finding are added here; see also the companion update to eg-local-administration-law-43-1979's own description in eg-cairo-municipal-finance.json.

reports.title: Citizen Investment Plan for Luxor Governorate (FY2023/2024)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Economic Development and International Cooperation (Egypt)
reports.description: A second governorate-level 'Citizen Investment Plan' data point, structurally identical to Cairo's existing eg-cairo-citizen-budget-2024-2025: a central-ministry document allocating public investment to a governorate, not a governorate-authored fiscal document. "Total Investment: 7.7 billion EGP", "Number of Projects: 201 developmental projects", described as "now in its fifth consecutive year of governorate-wide implementation." Like the Cairo plan, this document does not specify individual markaz, city, or administrative-subdivision-level detail — reinforcing rather than contradicting the pattern already documented for Cairo.
reports.cadence_note: Published annually per fiscal year, part of the same nationwide Citizen Investment Plan series as Cairo's.

reports.title: نظام الادارة المحلية (Local Administration System) — State Information Service
reports.publisher: State Information Service (SIS), Arab Republic of Egypt
reports.description: Egypt's official state information/media agency's own restatement of the Constitution's local-administration provisions, corroborating (from a genuine Egyptian government agency, not the OHCHR unofficial-translation mirror used for the Constitution's own text) that the independent-budget/elected-council design exists in law: "الدولة إلى وحدات إدارية تتمتع بالشخصية الاعتبارية، منها المحافظات، والمدن، والقرى" [The state is divided into administrative units enjoying legal personality, including governorates, cities, and villages]; "تنتخب كل وحدة محلية مجلساً بالاقتراع العام السرى المباشر، لمدة أربع سنوات" [Each local unit elects a council by direct secret public ballot for a four-year term]; "يكون للوحدات المحلية موازنات مالية مستقلة" [Local units shall have independent financial budgets]. IMPORTANT: this describes the system AS DESIGNED, not as currently operating — Local Popular Councils have been dissolved since 2011 (Law No. 116 of 2011) with no successor body elected since, so no independent local-unit budget publication exists in practice (consistent with eg-local-administration-law-43-1979's finding that sub-governorate 'resources' are statutorily governorate-allocated transfers, not autonomous budgets).
reports.cadence_note: Standing institutional/legal-system description page, not dated to a specific edition.

dependencies.basis: SIS's own description of the local-administration system directly restates Constitution Article 178's 'independent financial budgets' language, which eg-local-administration-law-43-1979's own description already documents as constitutionally promised but not implemented by the operative 1979 statute (whose Articles 43/51 make markaz/city 'resources' governorate-allocated transfers, not independent budgets) — SIS's page is the clearest primary-agency confirmation that this gap between constitutional design and statutory/operative practice is real and current.

_dropped.edge: Any individual markaz/madina/hay/qism -> a self-published sub-governorate budget document
_dropped.why: No sub-governorate budget or financial document was located for any Egyptian markaz, hay, or qism this round. New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA) cities (New Cairo, 6th of October) were also checked — NUCA is a national authority under the Ministry of Housing running parallel to, not nested inside, the governorate hierarchy, with presidentially-appointed 'city organs' rather than elected councils, so even a NUCA financial report (none located) would not represent this tier in the markaz/hay/qism sense.

_dropped.edge: Egypt's 2026 draft new Local Administration Law -> Cairo/sub-governorate finance
_dropped.why: Updates this file's own open question (eg-cairo-municipal-finance.json, eg-new-local-administration-law-draft): as of the latest evidence located this round (a 30 June 2026 news item still describing it as a 'مشروع قانون' / draft law), the bill remains unpassed after a decade of failed attempts (80 committee sessions since 2016 per an April 2026 report on Parliament's joint committee returning it to government over constitutional/substantive deficiencies). No primary parliamentary or government text of the draft itself was accessible (parlmany.com, dostor.org, masrawy.com bill-text pages all returned fetch errors). Still deferred, not resolved.
